title: The integers of a finite local-field extension are the integral closure
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $E\subseteq F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Give them their compatible extending $\ell$-adic absolute values, and put $\mathcal O_E=\{a\in E:|a|_E\leq1\}$ and $\mathcal O_F=\{x\in F:|x|_F\leq1\}$, as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Then, for every $x\in F$, $x\in\mathcal O_F$ if and only if $x$ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\mathcal O_E$. Equivalently, $\mathcal O_F$ is the integral closure of $\mathcal O_E$ in $F$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

source.place: First sentence, the arithmetic input on O_F/O_E: valuation/integral-closure bridge implicit in the finite-module assertion. A textbook treatment is Serre, Local Fields, Ch. II, section 2, Proposition 3 and its corollaries (wanted, not obtained).

proof.text: Put $K=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $A=\mathbf Z_\ell$. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $K$ is complete and $|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}<1$, so its norm is nontrivial. The compatible absolute values and valuation subrings are those of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]; [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value], applied to $F/K$, gives the ultrametric inequality on $F$. Choose a finite $K$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $F$, possible since $F/K$ is finite, with $d\geq1$ since a field is nonzero. Write $c_i(y)$ for the coordinates, so $y=\sum_i c_i(y)b_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-linear-homeomorphism] to the $K$-linear equivalence $F\to K^d$, $y\mapsto(c_i(y))_i$. Its hypotheses hold: $F$ and $K^d$ have Hausdorff norm/product topologies and continuous vector-space operations, because the absolute value on $F$ extends that on $K$ (scalar multiplication is field multiplication restricted to $K\times F$). Thus the coordinate map is continuous.

source.place: First sentence: supply the finite-dimensional coordinate topology for the arithmetic input; expanded agent argument

proof.text:
The inverse image under this coordinate map of $\{(a_i):|a_i|_\ell<1\ \text{for every }i\}$ is an open neighborhood of zero. Hence there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that $|y|_F<\varepsilon$ implies $|c_i(y)|_\ell<1$ for all $i$. Choose $N\geq0$ with $\ell^{-N}<\varepsilon$; this is possible since the geometric sequence $\ell^{-N}$ tends to zero. Fix $x\in\mathcal O_F$. For every $n\geq0$, including $n=0$, compatibility and multiplicativity give $|\ell^N x^n|_F=\ell^{-N}|x|_F^n\leq\ell^{-N}<\varepsilon$. Therefore $\ell^N c_i(x^n)=c_i(\ell^N x^n)$ belongs to $A$, using the unit-ball description in [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. It follows explicitly that
$$x^n=\sum_i(\ell^N c_i(x^n))(\ell^{-N}b_i)\in L:=\sum_i A(\ell^{-N}b_i).$$
Here the coordinate continuity is precisely that supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-linear-homeomorphism] in step 1. Thus all powers of $x$ lie in the single finitely generated $A$-module $L$; no uniform choice in $x$ is needed for the argument.

source.place: First sentence: explicit bounded-powers lattice argument, using the topology established in step 1

proof.text: The ring $A$ is a discrete valuation ring by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. In the definition [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], this is in particular an integral domain with every ideal principal. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] gives that $A$ is Noetherian. Let $B=A[x]\subseteq F$, concretely the set of all finite sums $\sum_{n=0}^m a_nx^n$ with $a_n\in A$. These sums contain $1$ and $x$ and are closed under addition, negation and multiplication by distributing finite sums, so $B$ is a commutative $A$-algebra and an $A$-submodule of $F$. Step 2 places every summand in $L$, hence $B\subseteq L$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] to the finitely generated $A$-module $L$ and its $A$-submodule $B$. This proves that $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module.

source.place: Tags 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr) and 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), submodule finiteness; PID Noetherianity is the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] to $A\to B$. Since $x\in B$, it satisfies a monic polynomial $P\in A[T]$, and the same equation holds in $F$ under the inclusion $B\hookrightarrow F$. For every $a\in A$, compatibility of the absolute value on $E$ with that on $K$ gives $|a|_E=|a|_\ell\leq1$, so $A\subseteq\mathcal O_E$, by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] and [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Regard the coefficients of $P$ as elements of $\mathcal O_E$. Its leading coefficient remains $1$, and evaluation in $F$ is unchanged, because $A\to E\to F$ is the given inclusion. Consequently $x$ is integral over $\mathcal O_E$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. This proves $x\in\mathcal O_F\Rightarrow x\text{ integral over }\mathcal O_E$.

source.place: Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral) and 00GI (definition-integral-ring-map); coefficient inclusion is the explicit elementary calculation

proof.text:
Conversely, suppose $x\in F$ is integral over $\mathcal O_E$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] there are $r\geq1$ and $a_0,\ldots,a_{r-1}\in\mathcal O_E$ with $x^r=-\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}a_jx^j$. Compatibility of absolute values and [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] give $|a_j|_F=|a_j|_E\leq1$. If $t=|x|_F>1$, repeated application of the ultrametric inequality of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] gives
$$t^r=\left|\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}a_jx^j\right|_F\leq\max_{0\leq j<r}(|a_j|_F t^j)\leq t^{r-1}<t^r,$$
a contradiction. Thus $|x|_F\leq1$, i.e. $x\in\mathcal O_F$. The two implications give the required equivalence for every $x$, and the definition of integral closure in [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] turns this pointwise equivalence into equality of the subrings.
